translations.text: These are the words that Moses spoke to all Israel beyond the Jordan, in the wilderness to the west, near the Red Sea, between Paran[?]Tophel and Laban and the Encampments and the Place of Gold.
It is an eleven-day journey from Horeb to Mount Seir, as far as Kadesh-barnea.
And I spoke to you at that time and said, “I cannot bear you alone.”
And how can I alone bear your troubles, your burdens, and your disputes?

Now where shall we go up? Your brothers have frightened your hearts, saying, “The people are great and numerous and stronger than we are, and the cities are very large and walled up to heaven. We also saw the sons of giants there.”
And we passed by our brothers, the sons of Esau who live in Seir, along the road of the Arabians, from Edom and Ezion-geber. Then we turned and passed along the road through the wilderness of Moab.
And now, Israel, listen to the statutes and judgments that I teach you today to carry out, so that you may live and enter and inherit the land that the Lord our God will give you.
And take great care of yourselves, for you saw no form on that day when the Lord spoke to you at Mount Horeb from the midst of the fire.
But God took you in hand and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be his own allotted people, as you are this day.
And the Lord will scatter you among all the nations, and you will remain few in number among the nations to which the Lord will take you.
And know today and take to heart that the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on the earth below, and there is no other besides him.
And Moses called all Israel and said to them, “Listen, Israel, to the statutes and judgments that I speak in your hearing this day. Learn them and be careful to carry them out.”
The Lord our God made a covenant with you at Horeb.

On the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God. On it you shall not do any of your work—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your ox, your donkey, any of your livestock, or the foreigner within your gates—so that your male servant and your female servant may rest as you do.
Go near yourself and hear whatever the Lord our God says. Then speak to us everything that the Lord our God speaks to you, and we will listen and do it.
If only they had such hearts within them, to fear me and keep my commandments every day, so that it might go well with them and their children forever!
And you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your strength.
Lest he turn your son away from me and he worship foreign gods, and the Lord become fiercely angry with you and destroy you quickly.
And you shall not bring the detestable thing into your house and become accursed like it. Rather, you shall utterly detest and abhor such things, for it is accursed.
Your clothes did not wear out on you, and your feet did not swell during those forty years.
And know today that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God gives you the good land to inherit, for you are a stiff-necked people.

And I stood in prayer before the Lord and said, “Lord, Lord, King of gods, do not destroy your people and your allotted possession, whom you redeemed by your great power, whom you brought out of Egypt by your great power, with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm.”
Behold, to the Lord your God belong the heavens and the heaven of heavens, the earth and everything in them.
You shall love the Lord your God and keep his observances, his statutes, his commandments, and his judgments all the days of your life.

You may slaughter animals and eat meat whenever you wish, according to the blessing the Lord your God has given you, in all your towns. Both the unclean and the clean among you may eat it together, as they would gazelle or deer.
When the Lord your God destroys before you the nations whose land you are entering to possess, and you take possession of their land and live in it,
There shall be no one in need among you, for the Lord your God will surely bless you in the land that the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance to possess.
For the Lord your God has blessed you as he promised you. You shall lend to many nations, but you shall not borrow. You shall rule over many nations, but they shall not rule over you.
Instead, you shall open your hand generously to him and lend him as much as he asks for in his need.
Observe the month of the first crops and celebrate the Passover to the Lord your God, for in the month of the first crops you came out of Egypt by night.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God at the place the Lord chooses: at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, the Festival of Weeks, and the Festival of Booths. You shall not appear before the Lord your God empty-handed.
You shall act according to the instruction given to you by those at the place the Lord your God chooses, and you shall be very careful to do everything as it is prescribed for you.
To serve the name of the Lord his God, like all his fellow Levites who stand there before the Lord God.
He shall eat his allotted share, apart from what each receives from the sale of family property.
Your eye shall have no pity on him: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
Any man who has become engaged to a woman but has not married her shall go back to his house, lest he die in battle and another man marry her.
Instead, you shall utterly devote them to destruction—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Girgashites—as the Lord your God commanded.
And you shall remove innocent blood from among you, if you do what is good and pleasing before the Lord your God.
If you are not pleased with her, you shall let her go free. You shall not sell her for money or treat her with contempt, because you have humiliated her.

Instead, he shall acknowledge the unloved woman's firstborn by giving him a double share of everything he possesses, because he is the first of his sons, and the right of the firstborn belongs to him.
If you see your brother's donkey or his ox fallen on the road, you shall not pass them by. Instead, you shall help him raise them up.
The girl's father shall say to the elders, “I gave this daughter of mine to this man as his wife, and he has come to hate her.”
You shall not speak peaceably with them all your days, forever.
You shall not bring a prostitute's wages or the price of a dog into the house of your God for any vow, for both are abominations before the Lord your God.
When you harvest olives, you shall not go back to gather the fruit left behind. It shall be for the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow.
If there is a dispute between people, they shall come before the court and be judged. The judges shall acquit the righteous and condemn the wicked.
The child who is born shall be established in the name of the deceased, so that his name may not be erased from Israel.
You shall cut off her hand, and your eye shall have no pity on her.
You shall not have in your bag two different weights, a large one and a small one.
And now, behold, I bring the firstfruits of the produce of the land that the Lord gave me, a land flowing with milk and honey. And you shall bow down there before the Lord your God.
And there you shall offer a sacrifice of deliverance to the Lord your God, and you shall eat and be satisfied there and rejoice before the Lord your God.
You shall take a wife, but another man shall take her away from you. You shall build a house, but you shall not live in it. You shall plant a vineyard, but you shall not harvest its fruit.
And they shall be signs and wonders upon you and upon your descendants forever.
Because you did not serve the Lord your God with joy and a sincere heart, despite your abundance of everything.

to give any one of them some of the flesh of his children, which he will eat because nothing is left to him in your distress and in the hardship with which your enemies will afflict you in all your cities.
And he shall bring upon you all the grievous diseases of the Egyptians, which you dreaded, and they shall lodge in you.
And the Lord shall bring upon you every illness and every affliction written in the book of these laws, until he destroys you.
And he led you through the wilderness for forty years. Your clothes did not grow old, and the shoes on your feet did not wear out.
but also with those who are here with us today before the Lord our God, and with those who are not with us today.

For I shall bring them into the good land that I swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey. They shall eat and be filled and satisfied, and they shall turn to foreign gods and serve them. They shall provoke me to anger and break the covenant that I made with them.
For I have called upon the name of the Lord. Give praise to the Lord our God.
God, whose works are true and all whose ways are just, is a faithful God, and there is no injustice in him. The Lord is righteous and blameless.
from the summits of the ancient mountains and from the tops of the everlasting hills.
And Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eyes had not grown weak, and his cheeks had not become wrinkled.
